newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo drops Brit Biotech asthma drug.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo drops Brit Biotech asthma drug.

text.p: British Biotech Plc said on Wednesday that Glaxo Wellcome Plc has decided to discontinue development work on a British Biotech oral asthma drug.
In a statement with first-quarter results, British Biotech said Glaxo Wellcome had been evaluating oral lexipafant as an alternative to using inhaled steroids in chronic asthma.

However, the company said Glaxo Wellcome's analysis of data from a Phase II, or intermediate stage, trial involving asthma sufferers "has shown that lexipafant oral induced no significant improvement in respiratory function compared to placebo".
British Biotech said it is continuing to run its own trials of oral lexipafant for multiple sclerosis. Glaxo had the right to take the asthma drug through approval and marketing stages.
An intravenous version of lexipafant for acute pancreatitis is widely exepected to be the group's first drug on the market.

Late stage, or Phase III, trials on the drug were completed in July, and British Biotech expects to release results of the trial in November, with a European marketing application submitted by the end of the first quarter of 1997.

British Biotech, which announced an expected widening of pretax losses in the three months to July 31 to 8.0 million stg from 7.0 million, also announced plans for late stage trials of anti-cancer drug Marimastat in lung, stomach and ovarian cancer and a mailignant form of brain cancer over the next six months.
Phase III trials of Marimastat on pancreatic cancer began in June 1996.
The drug is being compared directly with the best currently available drug for treating pancreatic cancer, Eli Lilly and Co's Gemzar.

British Biotech chief executive Keith McCullagh said in a statment that progress on Lexipafant and Marimastat in the first quarter was "very signifiant". Further news on both compounds would be available in November, he said.
